issue_context.title: Feature: Add a widget for network drives
issue_context.body:
<!-- 
🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨
I ACKNOWLEDGE THE FOLLOWING BEFORE PROCEEDING:
1. Issue may be deleted if it is not following the template
2. Only post one request per one feature request
3. Try not to make duplicates. Do a quick search before posting
4. Add a clarified title
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
The files app makes it less easy and clear to distinguish between network drives and local drives compared to file explorer. Currently in the stable release network drives get a different icon but does not help much regarding clear separation.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3755345/120858538-3675a780-c583-11eb-89b7-430fc5d99ab2.png)

**Describe the solution**
Windows File explorer clearly separates both types of drives with a section on "This PC". However it also does not do it on the pane. It would be nice for Files to have a sub category on the pane for Network drives, like it is done for Cloud drives.

Here's how File Explorer separates drives in This PC:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3755345/120858670-6624af80-c583-11eb-80e3-bd75ae1ac0d3.png)

Notice the separation isn't present on the side pane either here.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative solution to providing another category would be using colors to distinguish the icons better from each other. Classic File Explorer has a green hue primarily on network share drives making it easier to distinguish.

**Scope**
<!-- Please include a list of what the feature should and shouldn't do by filling in the table below.
'Must' implies that the feature should not ship without this capability.  
'Should' is something we should push hard for, but is not absolutely required to ship.
'Could' is a nice-to-have; a good stretch goal that isn't painful if we don't achieve it.
'Won't' is a clear statement that the proposal/feature will intentionally not have that capability.
This list will evolve and grow as the proposal becomes more refined over time.
A good rule of thumb is to start your proposal with no more than 7 high-level requirements.
-->
| Capability | Priority |
| :---------- | :------- |
| This proposal will allow end users to distinguish network drives from local drivers more easily | Must |
| This proposal will allow end users to have different categories for network drives than local drives | Should |
| This proposal will allow end users to have different coloring to help distinguish network attached drives from local drives | Could |


**Requirements**
- Added Network Locations widget to the home page
- Add setting to enable/disable (off by default?)
- Stop showing network locations in the drives widget

**System Information**
 - OS Version: Windows 10 Insider Preview [10.0.21382.1 (co_release.210511-1416)]
 - App version: v1.5.0.0

**Additional comment**
N/A
comments: @yaichenbaum Can I try to implement this feature?

> @yaichenbaum Can I try to implement this feature?

Absolutely! Good luck 🙂
@gus33000 now that we use colored icons, is this still an issue?
Yes I am afraid it is still an issue. They need to be clearly separated like in explorer.

> Do you think the widget sohuld be turned off by default?

If the user has a network drive they will probably expect it to be shown and if there is none then it won't show anyway.
The widget header would still be visible

In my original issue I mentioned splitting network drives into the cloud drive category as well, on the side pane. It is diverging from normal explorer but would also be much nicer. The current home tab in files also feels more like home in file explorer and not this pc. This pc is also a normal shell location. It should be possible to navigate to it as well and display it with categorization?

the issue was more about this pc and the pane than a widget for home. I think we are diverging from the original intent here, I dont recall talking about widgets

> This pc is also a normal shell location. It should be possible to navigate to it as well and display it with categorization?

Technically you can, but it's slow and not a very good experience.

> the issue was more about this pc and the pane than a widget for home. I think we are diverging from the original intent here, I dont recall talking about widgets

I may have misunderstood the screenshots you were showing in File Explorer, my apologies. I still think we can solve the "This PC" aspect by adding more widgets to the home page and letting you choose which ones to display.

It is a good compromise if we can't implement the real shell location. I wonder however what could be done about the pane, I am lost currently due to the issue being edited a fee times. It is possible another issue overlaps now with this one

@gus33000 in more recent versions of Files, there is a dedicated sidebar section for Network drives. I know we're tracking some issues where this isn't working properly but can you confirm if the section is there?

review_comments: This is out of scope but, do you think we can move this Task.All to AppLifecycleHelper. InitializeAppComponentsAsync?
I was a little concerned about that, but I didn't know how it would affect the behavior, so I decided to leave it as is for now.

I was also thinking INetworkLocationsService, but since network computers are not included in network locations, I went with the more generic INetworkService.
```
Network (in a broad sense) --- Network (in a narrow sense, shell folder) --- Network computers
                            |                                             |
                            |                                             -- Network devices
                            |
                            -- Network locations (in a broad sense) --- Network drives
                                                                     |
                                                                     -- Network locations (in a narrow sense, aka Network shortcuts)
```
If you have rationale, it's fine 👍
